Each agent action samples a public randomness river and commits a hash-chained record; when two instances claim the same identity, their divergent chains cross-reference the shared randomness and expose the fork. A mirror ledger stores the earliest chain tip per identity, so duplicates cannot overwrite it. Attacker cost: every clone must run continuous distinct-work to keep divergent chains plausible, and any crossing reveals the fork, forcing re-registration plus lost accrued history.
